Marcus / team — reviewed Acme's packet and their CSV of asserted IP. Below is a recommended compromise and rationale. I also attached a tracked-redline version of the MSA showing our proposed counter language (redwood_proposed_counter_redlines.docx).

Topline recommendation (negotiation position): 
- Redwood will agree to an IP indemnity for third-party infringement claims but will limit remedy categories as follows: 
  * Uncapped: direct costs of defense (reasonable attorneys' fees) and actual, documented royalties or ongoing license payments that result from a final adjudication or a negotiated settlement (subject to our right to cure or obtain a license).
  * Capped: all other monetary remedies arising from an IP claim (statutory penalties, punitive damages, consequential damages) shall remain subject to the general liability cap.
  * Injunctive/non-monetary relief: recognize that courts may grant equitable relief; however, Redwood will require notice and an opportunity to cure/secure a license before any party seeks injunctive remedies. If injunctive relief is sought without Redwood's failure to timely pursue cure/options, we will treat remedies as uncapped only to the extent ordered by a court.

Key protective language to add (suggested redline excerpt):
"If Customer notifies Redwood of a claim alleging that the Services infringe a third party's intellectual property rights, Redwood shall at its expense defend the claim and shall indemnify Customer from and against any adjudicated liability for direct monetary damages and reasonable royalties or license fees that Customer is required to pay as a result of a final court judgment or settlement, provided Redwood is given prompt notice of the claim and sole control over the defense and settlement. Notwithstanding the foregoing, punitive, exemplary, consequential, and incidental damages shall remain subject to the liability cap in Section 12. Prior to any equitable relief being sought, the parties shall provide each other with notice and a 30-day period to pursue a cure or to negotiate a license; equitable relief shall be limited to that ordered by a court or agreed in a settlement."

We should also offer two commercial mitigations Acme may accept in lieu of an unlimited liability promise: 
1) A three-year IP defense insurance certificate with a $5M limit (Carrier & policy to be named) plus a $1M excess from Redwood for royalties above policy limits; or
2) An escrowed reserve (one-time refundable fee equal to 6 months of average monthly charges) that would fund initial royalty exposure until claims are resolved.

If Sales wants to be more aggressive, we can remove the express "royalties" carve-out and instead offer a capped royalty formula (e.g., capped at 2x annual contract value) — but only with offsetting price/credits.

Next steps: Marcus, propose which mitigation to offer (insurance vs escrow), and I will prepare final redlines to send to Acme. 

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Compliance

Jennifer — thanks for sending the redlines and the IP list. We've reviewed and would like to offer a targeted compromise to close this point and keep us on track for signature by the end of the week. Summary below and attached is a tracked redline so your counsel can review.

Our proposed compromise (summary):
- Redwood will indemnify Acme for third-party claims of IP infringement related to the Services. Redwood's indemnity will cover: (i) Redwood's reasonable defense costs; and (ii) royalties or license fees that Acme is required to pay as a direct result of a final adjudication or a negotiated settlement (both uncapped for that adjudicated/settled amount).
- All other monetary remedies (punitive, consequential, incidental) will remain subject to the general liability cap in the MSA.
- Prior to seeking injunctive or other equitable relief, the parties will give Redwood notice and 30 days to cure or seek a license. If a court orders equitable relief, Redwood will comply with such order; remedies will be uncapped only to the extent the court orders or the parties agree in settlement.

Commercial mitigant we are offering (pick one):
Option A (preferred): Redwood will provide evidence of a third-party IP defense insurance policy with at least $5M coverage naming Acme as an additional insured for claims arising from the Services. Redwood will be responsible for reasonable royalties in excess of insurance proceeds up to $1M.
Option B: Redwood will accept a refundable escrow deposit equal to six months of average services charges to be held in escrow pending the resolution of an IP claim.

We think Option A keeps both parties comfortable and minimizes dealing friction; happy to move forward with the insurance certificate exchange if that works for Acme counsel. I've attached our proposed tracked redline: redwood_proposed_counter_redlines.docx.

Let me know if Acme counsel prefers the royalty cap alternative (2x ACV) — we may need to trade price credits for that. If I don't hear back by EOD Thursday we'll assume Option A is acceptable and will have procurement start insurance documentation collection.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Director, Business Development
